html:
The Treaty of Punakha was signed at Punakha on 8 January 1910 between Bhutan and British India. Bhutan agreed to be guided by Britain in its foreign relations, and Britain promised not to interfere in its internal affairs.

Britain wanted Bhutan as a buffer, worried about Chinese claims after the Qing pushed into Tibet. In return it doubled the yearly payment for the Duars, lost in the Duar War, and backed the new Wangchuck kings.

Bhutan, unlike the princely states, was never part of the British Raj, and so did not have to join India in 1947. A treaty with independent India in 1949 kept the same terms; it was rewritten in 2007 to drop the clause on foreign policy. Bhutan joined the United Nations in 1971.
sum: The Treaty of Punakha was signed at Punakha on 8 January 1910 between Bhutan and British India. Bhutan agreed to be guided by Britain in its foreign relations, and Britain promised not to interfere in its internal affairs.
